base_intake.interpretation: Canonical base intake is the preserved broad discovery baseline. It is not treated as a historical completeness proof.

within_year_temporal_skew_audit.diagnostic_slices: calendar quarters and months; audit-only, not publication units
within_year_temporal_skew_audit.assessment: No catastrophic temporal hole is visible in the base arXiv intake. All twelve months contain thousands of unique papers; Q4 is the densest quarter and Q1 the sparsest. The material completeness risk is capped dense categories plus present-day publisher-index archival loss, not an empty calendar interval.

arxiv_cap_audit.assessment: Ten month/category slices hit the configured 2,000-result ceiling. Base arXiv success therefore cannot establish research completeness. Material papers are checked by exact identity before annual Selection.

source_planes.notes: Base intake preserves InstructGPT, Chain-of-Thought, Self-Consistency, STaR, Minerva and ReAct primary papers, plus OpenAI's instruction-following release item. Exact identities are retained for annual normalization.

Base papers preserve LaMDA, Chinchilla, PaLM and OPT. Exact first-party Chinchilla, PaLM and OPT pages are added to preserve contemporary release/access framing that paper records alone do not fully express.

Base intake preserves DALL-E 2 lifecycle items and primary papers for DALL-E 2, Imagen, Flamingo, Parti, DreamFusion, Make-A-Video, Imagen Video and Phenaki. Stable Diffusion researcher/public release boundaries are absent from the base watchlist and require exact first-party gap-fill.

Base intake preserves OPT and BLOOM primary papers but not their exact contemporary access/release pages. Meta OPT and Hugging Face/BigScience BLOOM launch pages are added so research-access and open-access boundaries remain explicit.

Base intake preserves AlphaCode and ReAct papers plus OpenAI Codex-related official items. GitHub Copilot general availability is a material deployed coding-assistant event outside the configured base official-page watchlist; AlphaCode's first-party announcement is also retained for public chronology.

Base OpenAI feed preserves Whisper and ChatGPT exact launch items and base arXiv preserves Constitutional AI. DeepMind Sparrow is added as a first-party dialogue/safety/control research event with retrieval and rule-model boundaries.

Base intake preserves FlashAttention, HELM and BIG-bench primary papers. The configured GitHub release watchlist contributes no 2022 releases, which is recorded as a limitation rather than treated as proof that no relevant runtime milestones existed.

openai_rss.event: Aligning language models to follow instructions

residual_limitations: Present-day official index snapshots cannot prove that every 2022 publisher item remains linked or unchanged.
Ten capped arXiv month/category slices may omit non-headline research; exact checks protect material editorial anchors but do not make the full research intake exhaustive.

The configured GitHub release collector is oriented toward projects that became material later and returned no normalized 2022 release records; commit-level or non-Release runtime history is therefore not reconstructed exhaustively.
Some 2022 generative-media services and community projects have weak or mutable first-party archives; absence from current first-party indexes is not interpreted as historical absence.
First-party pages may have been edited after 2022; contemporary dates and launch states are preserved where the page itself exposes them, while later edits remain a hindsight limitation.

single_volume_preliminary_assessment.rationale: The year has a coherent annual arc across instruction/reasoning, compute-efficient scaling, multimodality/generative media, model access, deployed coding assistance, and late-year conversational/control systems. These planes interact strongly enough for a single annual synthesis; no split trigger is visible at coverage-audit stage.
